channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: The Conference Board's US consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September, its lowest since April 2014 and below the 89.2 economists had expected, with high energy prices among the reasons given.
item.description:
The August value was revised down to 88.6 from 89.4, according to Wallstreet:online, which attributes the decline partly to high energy prices. Dana Peterson, chief economist at the Conference Board, said consumers' appraisals of current business conditions turned negative for the first time since September 2024, and perceptions of the current labour market deteriorated but stayed positive, The Economic Times reports. Write-in responses, collected from 1 to 23 September, were mostly pessimistic, with frequent references to the high cost of goods, gas and services, according to the Chicago Tribune, which says the decline comes as wages stagnate and prices remain elevated amid the ongoing Iran war. The Straits Times reports that job openings fell to 7.079 million in August. The reporting does not give the expectations component or any measure of actual spending.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Confidence is a survey of sentiment, not a measure of spending, so the reading is a signal about demand rather than evidence of lower demand. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, weaker consumer confidence tends to reach durable purchases such as cars, furniture and home improvement first, which are end-markets for adhesive technologies, and the effect depends on whether spending data follow the survey. Points that may be worth considering include how US retail and do-it-yourself channels see demand for the fourth quarter, and whether automotive and furniture customers in the US adjust their production plans.

The Economic Times | Wallstreet:online | Chicago Tribune | The Straits Times

item.title: China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 in September from 49.8 in August, returning to expansion, with production up and new orders slightly lower, while the RatingDog survey reached a five-month high of 52.1.
item.description:
The official index from the National Bureau of Statistics showed the production sub-index up 1.3 points to 51.7 and new orders down 0.1 point to 50.5, according to China Daily and Commercial Times. The employment index fell 0.3 point to 48.4, and the raw material inventory index rose 0.1 point to 48.2. The index for large enterprises was unchanged at 50.6, medium enterprises rose to 49.7 and small enterprises to 48.9. The consumer goods industry read 50.7, equipment manufacturing 51.0 and high-tech manufacturing 52.5. The non-manufacturing PMI rose to 50.2 from 49.0. A separate survey, the RatingDog manufacturing PMI compiled by S&P Global, rose 0.6 point to 52.1, a five-month high, with its composite output index at 52.4. A reading above 50 indicates expansion. The reporting does not give export orders or price indices.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Both surveys point up in September, but the official index is only just above 50, production rose while new orders edged down, and small and medium firms remain below 50, so, on a general reading, the measure points to stabilisation rather than a broad recovery. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, equipment and high-tech manufacturing, the strongest segments, are where industrial and electronics adhesive technologies are used, while these figures do not isolate housing-related demand. Points that may be worth considering include whether new orders follow production upward in October, and how demand in Chinese industrial customer segments compares with the index.

China Daily | Commercial Times | Commercial Times

item.title: Chancellor Merz and the leaders of the Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, Austria and Finland threaten to withhold agreement on the EU's 2028–2034 budget unless the European Commission's proposed EUR 2 trillion is cut substantially.
item.description:
The six leaders want spending cuts of hundreds of billions of euros, and want to shift resources toward defence and innovative companies while reducing funding for farmers and poorer regions, which traditionally absorb around two-thirds of the EU budget, according to the Financial Times. The budget requires unanimous agreement among all 27 member states. The six countries account for around 40% of EU budget revenues, the Financial Times reports; China Daily puts the share at nearly 40% and says the demands are set out in a letter signed by the six heads of government. The reporting does not give the size of the cut the six are asking for as a single figure, the timetable of the negotiations, or the response of the Commission and of the countries that receive the most funding.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The letter is a negotiating position, not a decision, and on a general reading the budget process has far to run; unanimity means any member state can block the outcome. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, EU funding for poorer regions pays for a large share of public infrastructure and building work in Central and Eastern Europe, so a cut there, if agreed, would reach construction volumes in those countries after 2028, while more funding for defence and innovation would shift demand toward other industries. Points that may be worth considering include how much of the construction demand in Central and Eastern European markets depends on EU funding, and how the balance between regional and defence spending develops in the negotiations.

Financial Times | China Daily

item.title: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius plans to order 16 new A400M transport aircraft from Airbus to replace older machines, a purchase worth billions of euros that still needs approval by the Bundestag.
item.description:
The Bundeswehr currently has 53 A400Ms, all stationed in Wunstorf, according to Tagesschau. Die Zeit reports that 16 of them have no protection against missile attacks, and Wallstreet:online says the new aircraft are to replace older ones without tactical capabilities. Pistorius put the investment at a sum in the billions of euros. The defence magazine hartpunkt had earlier reported interest in 10 to 20 modernised A400Ms, and there are also considerations for a weapons-capable variant, which according to that report is not part of the current project, Die Zeit writes. The reporting does not give an exact cost, a delivery schedule, where the aircraft would be built, or when the Bundestag is expected to decide.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

This is a plan, not an order: the Bundestag still has to approve the purchase, and neither the exact price nor the timetable is known. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a follow-on order would extend production of an existing aircraft rather than start a new development, which may mean many of the materials used are already qualified. On a general reading, transport aircraft use adhesive technologies such as structural bonding and sealing materials in assembly and maintenance, so a longer production run supports existing aerospace supply relationships. Points that may be worth considering include when the Bundestag decision is likely, and whether an order changes production rates at the Airbus sites that build the aircraft.

Die Zeit | Tagesschau | Wallstreet:online

item.title: The US Navy has awarded Boeing a USD 20 billion contract to build the F/A-XX next-generation stealth fighter, beating Northrop Grumman, in a programme that could grow to hundreds of billions of dollars over its lifetime.
item.description:
The new jet is to have longer range and advanced stealth, and to work with uncrewed aircraft, according to The Straits Times; it is designed to replace the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet, which Boeing also builds for the Navy. Boeing won amid delays and congressional support, according to The Straits Times, and was viewed as a strong contender throughout the competition because of its long history of building carrier-based fighters. The programme could grow as production ramps up and potentially as international customers place orders. The reporting does not give the number of aircraft, the timetable for first flight or entry into service, the production sites, or the suppliers that will be involved. It also does not say what the USD 20 billion covers — development, first production lots or both. The Straits Times is the only source in today's reporting.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The award is a decision with a stated value, and the reporting says the programme could grow much larger, so, on a general reading, its effect on suppliers would run over many years. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, military aircraft of this type use composite structures, structural bonding and specialised surface technologies, and the materials are qualified early in development and then locked in for the life of the programme. Points that may be worth considering include when material qualification for the programme is likely to start, and which structural bonding and surface technologies in the aerospace portfolio are relevant to a naval fighter that replaces the F/A-18E/F.

The Straits Times

item.title: Japan's industrial output fell 1.7% in August from July, the second monthly decline, against a median forecast of a 1.7% rise, with motor vehicle production down 6.8% and business-oriented and general-purpose machinery down 6%.
item.description:
The figures come from the Ministry of Economy, and the forecast is the median of a Reuters poll, according to CNA. Business-oriented and general-purpose machinery output dropped 6% in August from July, and motor vehicle production dropped 6.8%. Manufacturers polled by the ministry expect seasonally adjusted output to climb 3.2% in September and 3.1% in October. In financial markets, Japan's two-year government bond yield rose to 1.975%, the highest since March 1995, a rise attributed to expectations that the Bank of Japan could take a more hawkish stance to support the yen, after it raised its policy rate to 1.25% earlier in September, according to The Economic Times. The reporting does not give year-on-year changes, the reasons for the decline in vehicle and machinery output, or inventory levels.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The fall is measured against the previous month, and manufacturers expect a rebound in September and October, so the next two releases show whether August was a dip or a turn. Vehicles and business-oriented and general-purpose machinery both fell well more than the overall index, and, on a general reading, both are customer industries for adhesive technologies. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, month-on-month vehicle output in Japan can swing with production stoppages and model changes, which the reporting does not mention. Higher short-term interest rates, on a general reading, raise financing costs for investment in machinery and construction. Points that may be worth considering include whether the rebound manufacturers expect appears in September, and how Japanese automotive and machinery customers plan production for the rest of the year.

CNA | The Economic Times

item.title: UK vehicle production rose 5.7% in August on a year earlier to 40,872 units, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT), with car output up 6.1% to 39,328 units, the strongest rise since December 2025.
item.description:
Output for the domestic market rose 26.0% in August, while production for export rose 1.4%; exports accounted for 77.1% of all cars made in the month, according to SMMT. The rise in car production was the strongest since December 2025. The summary of the SMMT release does not give commercial vehicle output separately, year-to-date totals, the split by powertrain, or the reasons for the stronger home-market output. It also does not name the manufacturers or plants behind the increase. The SMMT is the only source in today's reporting.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rise is measured and comes mainly from output for the home market, while export production, which still makes up more than three-quarters of cars built, rose only slightly. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a single month's figure says little about the trend without later months. Also on a general reading, adhesive technologies in vehicle assembly, from structural bonding to sealing and interior applications, follow the number of vehicles built, so UK volumes matter to suppliers with local plant business. Points that may be worth considering include whether the September and October figures confirm the direction, and how UK export production develops, given that exports made up 77.1% of cars built in August.

SMMT

item.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics will invest KRW 4.27 trillion in package substrate capacity in Korea, and Broadcom and Toppan have opened Singapore's first FC-BGA substrate plant, as Taiwanese packaging and test groups extend expansion into 2027 for AI chips.
item.description:
Samsung Electro-Mechanics announced the Korean investment on 28 September for its Sejong factory, with an investment period to 31 May 2028 and mass production planned from September 2028; the amount equals 43.6% of the company's equity at the end of 2025, according to SEMI China. Its Vietnamese subsidiary announced a further KRW 2.51 trillion for local substrate facilities. In Singapore, Broadcom and the Japanese printing technology group Toppan unveiled Advanced Substrate Technologies on 29 September, the first factory in the country able to produce flip chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrates, which will create more than 330 new jobs, according to Lianhe Zaobao. In Taiwan, ASE aims to double its advanced packaging and testing revenue in 2027, Powertech plans to mass-produce panel-level packaging and co-packaged optics, and King Yuan is investing TWD 50 billion in AI chip testing capacity, Commercial Times reports. In Europe, the Global Electronics Association has signed a memorandum with the Fraunhofer Group for Microelectronics to help accelerate the path from advanced packaging innovation to industry-scale manufacturing, with a focus on APECS, the EU Chips Act pilot line for advanced packaging. The reporting does not give capacity volumes, customers or the Singapore investment amount.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Most of the steps are quantified, and they place new capacity in Korea, Vietnam, Singapore and Taiwan, with mass production at the Korean Sejong plant planned from September 2028. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, substrates and advanced packages rely on materials such as underfills, die-attach adhesives and thermal interface materials, so new packaging lines are where adhesive technologies for electronics are specified and qualified. Also on a general reading, qualification in semiconductor packaging takes a long time, which means material choices for lines starting in 2028 may be made well before then. Points that may be worth considering include the timing of qualification work with substrate and packaging makers building new lines, and whether local supply and technical service are available in Vietnam and Singapore.

SEMI China | Lianhe Zaobao | Commercial Times | Commercial Times | Global Electronics Association

item.title: Turnover in Germany's main construction industry rose 4.6% in real terms in July on a year earlier and new orders fell 1.9% after price adjustment, and the ZDB says a gap in funding until summer 2027 can no longer be ruled out.
item.description:
The figures come from the Federal Statistical Office and were published by the Central Association of the German Construction Industry (ZDB). The number of employees in July was 1.5% above the level of a year earlier. Felix Pakleppa, the ZDB's general manager, says the situation in the construction sector remains fragile and that the next setback is imminent at the turn of the year: the special funding for EH-55 new buildings will expire at the latest at the end of 2026, cuts to the new-building budget are in the pipeline for 2027, and no one yet knows what funding will look like from January. The reporting does not split the figures between residential, commercial and civil engineering construction, state the period against which the 1.9% fall in orders is measured, give month-on-month changes, or state the size of the planned budget cuts. It also does not say how many projects depend on the EH-55 funding or how large the order backlog is. The ZDB is the only source in today's reporting.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Turnover and orders measure different stages: on a general reading, turnover reflects work on orders already won, while new orders point to the volume of work in the months ahead, so a rise in the first together with a fall in the second, if both are measured on the same base, is a signal about the later part of the year rather than about July. The ZDB links the risk to a policy date, the end of the EH-55 funding, which, on a general reading, is a German efficiency standard for new buildings. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, new residential building uses a wide range of adhesive technologies, from flooring and tile adhesives to sealants and insulation bonding, so a funding gap in new-build could shift demand toward renovation. Points that may be worth considering include how German construction distributors see order books for the first half of 2027, and which product lines depend more on new-build than on renovation.

ZDB

item.title: China will subsidise mortgage interest for eligible first-time homebuyers by one percentage point a year from 1 October, the first central-government subsidy on commercial housing loans, and the central bank has cut its one-year PSL rate to 1.5%.
item.description:
The Ministry of Finance, the People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration issued the joint notice on 29 September, according to Xinhua. The subsidy is an annualised one percentage point for up to five years (on the mortgage principal, BNN Bloomberg says); the maximum subsidised loan is CNY 1 million, and the implementation period is tentatively one year. BNN Bloomberg reports that the home should have a floor area of up to 120 square metres and a price of up to CNY 1.5 million to qualify; Xinhua says the policy focuses on first-time buyers with essential needs buying relatively low-priced, small and medium-sized homes. The People's Bank cut the rate on its pledged supplementary lending (PSL), which the South China Morning Post says is meant to better incentivise policy banks to support the real economy, by 25 basis points from 1.75% to 1.5%, and broadened it to investment in water, power-grid, computing, communications, urban pipeline and logistics networks, according to MarketScreener; it also raised several relending quotas, including the one for sci-tech innovation and technological upgrading by CNY 200 billion to CNY 1.4 trillion. The day before, a State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang had proposed to research and introduce measures to stabilise the real estate market. The reporting does not give the total cost of the subsidy, the number of eligible buyers, or an expected effect on sales or construction starts.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The subsidy works on the cost of buying rather than on the supply of homes, and it is limited to first-time buyers of smaller, lower-priced homes, so its reach depends on how many buyers fall inside the caps. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, when a market carries a large stock of unsold homes, extra purchases are likely to absorb that stock before they lead to new construction starts, so any effect on building volumes may come later than the effect on sales. The broadening of the PSL facility to water, power-grid, pipeline and logistics networks points to infrastructure rather than housing. On a general reading, both channels reach adhesive technologies in China through construction, the first through fit-out and renovation of purchased homes and the second through civil works. Points that may be worth considering include whether October sales data show a response in the capped segment, and which construction channels in China would see a change first.

Xinhua | BNN Bloomberg | South China Morning Post | MarketScreener | Commercial Times

item.title: Generic environmental claims such as "eco-friendly" and "biodegradable" are banned in the EU from 27 September unless the trader can show recognised excellent environmental performance, the Australasian Bioplastics Association (ABA) reports.
item.description:
The ABA, citing the EU change, warns that Australia could become a dumping ground for vague claims of this kind. Australia has no specific rule for compostable and biodegradable claims, according to the association. Its chief executive, Martine Poulain, says bags, food service ware and packaging labelled "biodegradable" or "eco-friendly" with nothing to back the claim are already appearing on Australian shelves. The account of the EU rule comes from the association's release; no other outlet in today's reporting covers it. The release does not name the EU legal act, explain what counts as recognised excellent environmental performance or how a trader proves it, say whether claims tied to a named certification or standard remain allowed, or describe how and by whom the ban is enforced in the member states. It also does not say whether products and packaging already on the market before 27 September are affected, or give any estimate of how many products carry such claims.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading, the rule concerns what may be claimed rather than what a product or its packaging is made of, so its first effect is likely on labels, marketing and the evidence behind them. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, the EU ban belongs to consumer-protection rules on green claims, and a brand that wants to keep an environmental claim needs evidence for it, which can pass down the supply chain as requests for data on each component, including adhesives, labels and coatings in the pack. Also on a general reading, claims such as compostability or recyclability of a pack can depend on the adhesive used in it, so adhesive technologies suppliers to packaging may be asked to document how their products affect those claims. Points that may be worth considering include which environmental claims on the business's own products and packaging in the EU use generic terms, and what documentation packaging customers may request to support claims on their packs.

Australasian Bioplastics Association

item.title: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche has instructed the federally owned energy company Sefe to increase natural gas storage, in a step coordinated with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Handelsblatt reports, citing ministry sources.
item.description:
The instruction was given on Tuesday evening, according to the ministry sources quoted by Handelsblatt, which describes it as the next step to further secure Germany's gas supply. In mid-September the minister had already urged the federal gas importer to buy gas to fill the storage facilities, but at that time it was explicitly not an instruction to Sefe, as the company had officially announced. This time, according to the report, it is an instruction. The report does not give the volume Sefe is to inject, a target fill level, the current level of German storage, the price at which gas is to be bought, who carries the cost, or the period over which the storage is to be filled. It also does not say whether other storage operators or importers are asked to act, or what prompted the timing beyond the aim of securing supply. No other outlet in today's reporting covers the step, so the account rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The step is a supply-security measure rather than a price measure: on a general reading, it may add buying by a state-owned company while storage is being filled, and the reporting gives no indication of how large that buying is. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, extra state-directed purchases before winter can add to demand in the wholesale gas market while they last, and fuller storage can reduce the risk of shortages later in the heating season. Also on a general reading, natural gas is both an energy source and a raw material for the German chemical industry, so the balance between supply security and wholesale prices reaches producers of raw materials for adhesive technologies as well as their own plants. Points that may be worth considering include how much of the gas used at German sites is bought on contract against short-term prices over the coming winter, and which operations are exposed if wholesale gas prices move while storage is being filled.

Handelsblatt
